scope_note: Opened primary PDFs are reference_section. Indexed primary content remains stored_search_excerpt when the page open returned CAPTCHA or failed. Established atom conversion is separated from disputed microscopic intermediate assignments.

evidence.title: Unique Biradical Intermediate in the Mechanism of the Heme Enzyme Chlorite Dismutase
evidence.retrieved_excerpt: two weakly coupled amino acid cation radicals
evidence.read_sections: Abstract, introduction, native-substrate rapid kinetics, EPR interpretation, proposed cycle and conclusion; public 12-page publisher PDF at an author institution.
evidence.finding: Native chlorite turnover gives transient ferric-state and radical signals different from the peracetic-acid model reaction. The authors propose a protein-biradical intermediate and confined oxygen recombination, revising a compulsory Compound-I route.
evidence.limits: Compound T identity and assignments of heme-bound species are mechanistic interpretations, not atom-resolved captures of the complete trajectory. Later calculations dispute the stable starting adduct. The row therefore specifies established intramolecular atom conversion without declaring I, II or T the unique intermediate.
evidence.boundary: Catalase cycles between two peroxide molecules and oxidizes an existing O–O unit; chlorite has two Cl–O bonds and creates a new O–O bond while its chlorine is reduced. Photosystem II couples light-driven oxidizing-equivalent accumulation to water oxidation. Molybdenum oxygen transfer requires an external reductive reset; heme–Cu oxidase cleaves O2 with incoming reducing equivalents. None describes this internally balanced chlorite rearrangement. Changing organism, oligomerization, or preferred intermediate hypothesis does not create another card.

supplementary.title: Mechanism of and exquisite selectivity for O–O bond formation by the heme-dependent chlorite dismutase
supplementary.retrieved_excerpt: originates entirely from chlorite and not from solvent water
supplementary.finding: Indexed primary discussion reports ion chromatography and mass-spectrometric 1:1 chloride/O2 conversion and isotope support for chlorite-derived oxygen. Its Compound-I/hypochlorite mechanism relied partly on a surrogate oxidant and is not adopted as established fact. PMC open returned a challenge.

supplementary.title: Molecular Mechanism of Enzymatic Chlorite Detoxification: Insights from Structural and Kinetic Studies
supplementary.retrieved_excerpt: Compound I and hypochlorite do not recombine
supplementary.finding: Opened primary PDF reports stopped-flow, optical/Raman and crystal/neutron data. Compound II dominated native turnover under its conditions, challenging the older Compound-I rebound model. Arg remains protonated at high pH, so its simple acid-base titration is not assumed to explain all activity changes.

supplementary.title: No heme-chlorite adduct in the catalytic cycle of chlorite dismutase: Insight from QM/MM and dynamics calculations
supplementary.finding: Indexed 2026 primary computational abstract questions a stable iron–chlorite adduct and favors a ferryl state with delocalized radical character. This limits microscopic certainty; it does not refute the established chlorite-to-chloride/O2 reaction. PubMed open returned CAPTCHA.

excluded_candidates.primary_title: Mechanism of Action of Flavin-Dependent Halogenases
excluded_candidates.reason: Final chemistry is already covered by the electrophilic-aromatic-substitution parent. A lysine chloramine carrier is disputed versus hydrogen-bond-guided HOCl, and N-halamine storage is already present. A new enzyme or directed position does not supply a sufficiently independent route here.

editorial_attention: Accepted as a distinct atom-rearrangement and internal redox coupling. The full elementary sequence remains unresolved; explicit qualification is essential. No earlier excluded PEP, membrane-gap or QueE candidate was revived.
